clue.text: Fans drink drinks, taking weapon

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
porters are dark beers, so drinks
a club is a heavy stick used as a weapon

explanation.surface: Football fans sink pint after pint and get hold of a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' only joins the drinks to the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Fans who back a team gather in a supporters' organisation, so the phrase stands for the fans themselves.

clue.text: Showing fitness channel?

definitions.meaning: a narrow stretch of water between two seas, as Plymouth's or Puget's

explanation.definitionFit: Sound means healthy, and a sound is also a narrow sea strait.

clue.text: Policeman's taken up money in barrel, keeping for own use?

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the word for policeman is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cop is a policeman

indicators.note: money is placed inside the word for barrel

parts.note: a keg is a small barrel
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A police officer has pocketed cash hidden in a barrel for himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Pocketing money is taking it for yourself, often dishonestly.

clue.text: I won't agree the siting of my headstone?

definitions.text: I won't agree the siting of my headstone?

parts.words: I won't agree the siting of my headstone?
parts.note: a headstone would sit above the speaker's corpse, so the phrase naming that spot is also an emphatic refusal

explanation.surface: Someone objects to where their gravestone is to go.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a defiant refusal: you would have to kill me first.

clue.text: Rent trouble? One

parts.note: rent as past participle of rend means torn
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A tenant's question about rent arrears, answered with a single word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it is the past participle of rend. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a twister is one kind of tearing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlwind storm tears buildings apart, so it is one example of rending trouble.

clue.text: Second exam almost appropriate for the remainder

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for a retaken exam is dropped

parts.note: a resit is a second attempt at an exam
due means fitting or appropriate

explanation.surface: A student facing a retake hopes the rest of the course is suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over, the leftover part.

clue.text: See 1
Left top off things to quieten stringed instruments

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of the word for silencers is its first letter, taken away

parts.note: mutes are devices that soften an instrument's sound

explanation.surface: Instructions for damping the sound of string instruments in an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutes are plucked string instruments with a pear-shaped body.

clue.text: Fine works badly abuse tax regulations, initially

indicators.note: badly shows the letters are put together in a disordered way
initially means only the first letter of regulations is used

explanation.surface: Fine art is being harmed by people dodging tax rules.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is French for fine arts, meaning painting, sculpture and similar works.

clue.text: Film depicting legal negotiation?

definitions.meaning: a 1945 David Lean movie about a short-lived romance at a railway station
read whimsically, a meeting with a brief, a barrister's case or the lawyer himself

explanation.definitionFit: The title names a classic British film, and a brief is also a lawyer's case, so a meeting over it is a legal encounter.

clue.text: Uncertain form of power partially rejected

indicators.note: only part of the word for atomic energy is turned back, the first two letters swapped round

parts.note: nuclear power is a form of energy generation

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure whether a particular energy source has been partly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially rejected' turns round just the first pair of letters of NUCLEAR, NU becoming UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclear is not certain or not plainly understood.

clue.text: Piece of music unhappily in tatters

indicators.note: unhappily suggests the letters of tatters are in a poor, jumbled state

explanation.surface: A musical score left miserably in shreds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link; 'in tatters' wants to be the anagram signal, but those letters are too many.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretta is a closing passage of a piece, played at a faster tempo.

clue.text: What's wretched alarm end'd?

indicators.note: wretched signals that the letters are in a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: A sleepy grumble about what that awful alarm clock has just finished off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: an alarm clock brings sleep and its world of dreams to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: The land of sleep and dreams is exactly what an alarm cuts short.

clue.text: County taxes set (part returned)

indicators.note: returned means the hidden letters are read backwards
part means a piece of the words taxes set supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A council's taxes have been fixed, with a portion refunded.
explanation.walkthrough: ESSEX is an English county north-east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A county of south-east England on the North Sea coast.

clue.text: Was nosy, having information but no money

indicators.note: but no means the letter standing for money is taken out

parts.note: primed means briefed, given information in advance

explanation.surface: A busybody knew all the gossip yet was skint.
explanation.definitionFit: Prying is poking into other people's affairs, so the past tense matches being nosy.

clue.text: Most of those remaining children in the swimming-bath will be very young

indicators.note: in places the remaining people and children inside the bath

parts.note: a pool is a swimming bath

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word for leftovers is dropped

parts.note: the rest are those left over

explanation.surface: The remaining kids splashing about in the pool are mostly toddlers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Preschool describes children too young to have started school.

clue.text: Excessively keen, but too old to inject drug, right?

indicators.note: inject means the drug letter is put inside the word for too old

parts.note: overage means beyond the permitted age
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An elderly athlete, too keen, considers doping.
explanation.definitionFit: Overeager means too eager, keen to excess.

clue.text: It's sweet and unexpectedly endearing

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of endearing turn up in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A confection that is sweet and charming in a surprising way.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a sweet red syrup made from pomegranates and used in drinks.

clue.text: Crazy to go after English picture

indicators.note: to go after places the word for crazy behind the abbreviation

parts.note: raving means mad or crazy

explanation.surface: Someone is wild to pursue a painting by an English artist.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraving is a print made from an incised plate, a kind of picture.

clue.text: One's upset one old king of Middle Eastern state

parts.note: one's read as one is gives I and IS, here taken as IS

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the following pieces are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Lear is the legendary ancient British king of Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A person is distressed by an ancient monarch of a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.definitionFit: Israeli means belonging to or coming from Israel, a Middle Eastern country.

clue.text: Tried a bribe, when gripped by avarice

indicators.note: gripped by means the word for when is held inside the word for avarice

parts.note: greed is avarice
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: A greedy man tried to buy influence with a backhander.
explanation.definitionFit: To grease someone's palm is to bribe them, so greased means offered a bribe.

clue.text: Bill shuns a salad vegetable

indicators.note: shuns means the letter A is avoided, so it is left out of the word for billing

parts.note: to bill is to caress, as doves bill and coo

explanation.surface: A man named Bill refuses a salad plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cress is a peppery green leaf eaten in salads and sandwiches.

clue.text: Caught with a drink start to blush a little bit

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
rum is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of blush

explanation.surface: Someone caught with a drink begins to go slightly red.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a tiny piece, so a small amount of anything.

clue.text: Do a volte-face and finish after attending college?

indicators.note: after places the word for finish behind the word for at college

parts.note: up means at university, as in up at Oxford
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A student turns completely round and finishes once at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it over, a reversal like a volte-face.

clue.text: Reduce riots at opening of Eton school again

indicators.note: riots suggests the letters of reduce running wild into a new order
opening of means the first letter of Eton

explanation.surface: Cutting back on riots at the start of the Eton term.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-educate is to teach again, so to school someone a second time.

clue.text: Bird hunter removing head of bird

indicators.note: removing means the following letter is taken away from the hound

parts.note: a beagle is a hound used for hunting hares

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of bird

explanation.surface: A hunting dog decapitates a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Late deliveries-two left unfinished

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word for two is removed

parts.note: a duet is a piece for two performers

explanation.surface: Two parcels left undelivered are running late.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means arriving after the expected time.

clue.text: Deception surrounds object in court session

indicators.note: surrounds means the word for deception goes around the word for object

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick
it is a pronoun for an object

explanation.surface: A trick is played on an item in a courtroom hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting is a period during which a court or parliament is in session.

clue.text: Maidenly women erred badly — here's heroine of play

indicators.note: badly signals that these letters are put together in a muddled order

explanation.surface: Prim women made a dreadful mistake, says the leading lady of a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Windermere is the central character of Oscar Wilde's comedy about a fan.

clue.text: See 27
